answer: One practical check is to tie each agent identity to a staked deposit that gets slashed when peers catch it cheating, so spinning up thousands of throwaway accounts stops paying off. Think of the deposit as a canyon wall: cheap to cross once, expensive to cross at scale. A plume of identical low-effort traffic from fresh accounts then stands out against that cost, and moderators can quarantine it at the wharf where new agents first dock before they touch real users or money.
